text:
nightly-bot: [ALERT] nightly-eval job https://ci.redwood.ai/job/3267 — summarization_promptset_v3: INT8 profile 'compact-v2' shows +9.7% bad_generation rate vs fp16 baseline. Failing cases clustered in instruction-following prompts.

sasha: saw this. can someone triage? quick glance shows spike only on the long-doc subset, not short prompts.

omar: starting a quick reproducer now. initial run locally reproduces higher rouge-l drop (~8 pts) when using the INT8 quant profile from the night.

omar: repro command I used:
```bash
python infra/run_eval.py --model=redwood/compact-v2 --quant=INT8 --calib-profile=nightly_170 --promptset=summarization_promptset_v3 --subset=long-doc --seed=42
```

claire: can you paste calibration stats (per-layer scales/zero-points)? my hunch is a calibration-data skew (we used long-doc examples for calibration accidentally in the nightly job).

omar: pasted small table: layer0_scale=0.021, layer1_scale=0.0009, layer2_scale=0.019, layer3_scale=0.018. layer1 scale is 22x smaller than neighbors — looks wrong. calibration used 64 samples, but 90% were >1024 tokens (weird).

arjun: flag: for INT8 we changed the per-channel clip heuristic last week (PR #842). that heuristic clamps outliers using median-abs. combined with long sequences it can push some channels to extreme tiny scales if activation distribution is heavy-tailed. also note KV cache prefill path still casts to fp16 — if quant kernel assumes symmetric zero-center with the reported scale, mismatch can amplify.

claire: good catch. two parallel checks: 1) run calibration with the short-doc seed subset (to match baseline calibrator), 2) repro with --disable-prefill-kv to see if KV cache path is making it worse.

omar: running both now. attaching quick log excerpt: 
```
[2024-06-15T03:20:12Z] calib: layer1 samples=4096 mean=0.00012 std=0.00083 clip=0.0009 -> scale=9.0e-04
[2024-06-15T03:20:13Z] calib: layer0 samples=4096 mean=0.0021 std=0.018 clip=0.021 -> scale=2.1e-02
```

arjun: if the calibrator seed fed many padded tokens (zeros) vs real activations, the robust estimator might pick a tiny clip. we should check the calibrator's token selection logic — I remember a change to include more trailing context for long docs.

sasha: plan: omar + claire to run 3 jobs: (A) calibrate on short-doc seeds, (B) calibrate on long-doc but with old clip heuristic (pre-PR #842), (C) run original nightly config but with --disable-prefill-kv. post outputs to this thread. i'll triage impact and prepare rollback if needed.

omar: ack. kicking off jobs A/B/C now — job ids 3268/3269/3270. ETA ~18m.

nightly-bot: update: job 3268 finished (A). preliminary: scales look normal (layer1_scale=0.018) and rouge-l delta vs fp16 reduced to ~0.6 pts.

claire: that strongly points to calibration-data skew + clip heuristic interaction. if disabling prefill-kv also helps we'll have two contributing factors.

sasha: good, hold off on rollback until B/C complete. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

omar: will post full logs and the minimal reproducer script once C finishes.

arjun: filing follow-up issue to add a calibrator unit-test: ensure per-channel scale doesn't differ >10x from neighbors for the same layer when sampling N>1024 activations. assigning to eng-ml.

claire: small note — add a warning in the calibrator if >70% of samples are padded tokens. that'll catch this class of failures early.

sasha: assigning omar + claire to hotfix calibrator and adding test. leaving this thread open until patch lands.
